experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes
experiences.description: Hit the world-class ski slopes of the Jungfrau region, covering Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. With over 200km of groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels, families can enjoy beginner-friendly runs while experienced skiers tackle challenging black runs with breathtaking Eiger views.

experiences.name: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride
experiences.description: Board the legendary Glacier Express panoramic train connecting Zermatt to St. Moritz. This iconic 8-hour journey crosses 291 bridges and 91 tunnels through stunning Alpine scenery, frozen valleys, and snow-capped peaks — a magical and relaxing family experience requiring no physical exertion.
experiences.location: Zermatt to St. Moritz, Valais & Graubünden

experiences.name: Family Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking
experiences.description: Explore the serene winter landscape around Saas-Fee on a guided family snowshoeing tour. Trails wind through snow-laden pine forests and open Alpine meadows, with guides sharing local wildlife and mountain ecology knowledge. Equipment rental is included and trails are suitable for children aged 6 and up.

experiences.name: Swiss Cheese & Fondue Cooking Experience
experiences.description: Join a hands-on traditional Swiss fondue and raclette cooking class in a cozy Alpine chalet. Learn the art of preparing authentic Swiss cheese dishes using local Gruyère and Appenzeller, paired with regional wines and warm bread. A delicious cultural immersion perfect for the whole family.

experiences.name: Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run
experiences.description: Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling natural toboggan runs, stretching over 3km through Alpine forest and open snowfields. Rent traditional wooden sleds and race down the mountain as a family, with a cozy mountain hut at the bottom serving hot chocolate and local pastries to warm up afterward.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly train from Zurich HB to Grindelwald via Interlaken Ost (approx. 2.5–3 hrs, use Swiss Travel Pass or buy a saver ticket in advance). Check into your boutique stay in Grindelwald-Wengen. Take a relaxed stroll through Grindelwald village, admire the iconic views of the Eiger North Face, and get oriented with the local area, ski rental shops, and lift stations.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the village center on foot. Visit the Grindelwald Tourist Office to pick up free maps, ski passes info, and discount tips. Settle in and unpack.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or on the train — pack snacks or grab a budget sandwich from a Migros or Coop kiosk at Zurich Airport.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable meal at the Coop Restaurant in Interlaken Ost during your train connection (budget CHF 12–16).
meals.dinner: Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald — a cozy, affordable local restaurant offering Swiss classics like rösti and fondue at reasonable prices (budget CHF 20–28 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 7-day Jungfrau Ski Region pass in advance online for the best rates. Consider the Swiss Half Fare Card if you plan multiple train trips. Migros and Coop supermarkets are your best friends for budget breakfasts and snacks throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: First full ski day! Head to the Grindelwald-First ski area, one of the most accessible and family-friendly ski zones in the Jungfrau Region. Beginners and families can enjoy the gentle slopes at First, while more experienced skiers can tackle the longer red and blue runs. Ski rental is available at Sport Bödeli or Intersport in the village — book ahead online for discounts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the First slopes. Families with children can take advantage of the dedicated kids' ski school area near the First gondola base. Try the First Cliff Walk (free with gondola access) for breathtaking panoramic views of the Bernese Alps during a mid-afternoon break.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village by gondola. Warm up with a hot chocolate or glühwein at a local café. Relax at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at your boutique stay using groceries from Coop or Migros (bread, cheese, cold cuts, yogurt — budget CHF 5–8 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the supermarket to eat on the mountain (sandwiches, fruit, thermos of soup — budget CHF 8–12 per person) to save significantly vs. mountain restaurants.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Pizzeria Alpenrose in Grindelwald — hearty pizzas and pasta at budget-friendly prices (CHF 18–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Ski rental tip: Renting from village shops is cheaper than on-mountain rentals. Helmet rental is strongly recommended, especially for children. First gondola opens around 8:30 AM — arrive early to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Take the scenic Wengernalp Railway (WAB) from Grindelwald to Kleine Scheidegg — a stunning mountain train journey with views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. Ski the famous Lauberhorn and Kleine Scheidegg area, which connects Grindelwald and Wengen ski zones. This is a highlight of the Jungfrau ski region with diverse runs for all levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski down toward Wengen via the long Lauberhorn descent (one of the world's most famous downhill race courses). Explore the car-free village of Wengen for an hour — a charming, peaceful Alpine village. Take the cog railway back up to Kleine Scheidegg and ski back toward Grindelwald.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald via train. Visit the Grindelwald ice rink (Sportzentrum) for an affordable family ice skating session (approx. CHF 8–12 per person including skate rental).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation (oatmeal, toast, eggs — budget CHF 4–7 per person).
meals.lunch: Self-Service Restaurant at Kleine Scheidegg station — more affordable than full-service mountain restaurants. Try the soup and bread combo (budget CHF 14–18 per person).
meals.dinner: Supermarket dinner night — buy ready-made meals, raclette cheese, potatoes, and cold cuts from Migros for a fun self-catered raclette night at the accommodation (budget CHF 10–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Wengernalp Railway is included in the Jungfrau Ski Region pass. Wengen is car-free — a lovely contrast to Grindelwald. The Lauberhorn run is long and best suited for intermediate to advanced skiers; beginners should stick to Kleine Scheidegg area slopes.

day_by_day.morning: Family snow activity day! Head to the Grindelwald-First area for non-ski winter fun. Try the First Flyer (a thrilling zip line over the Alps, approx. CHF 29 per person) or the Snowcat family snowshoeing trail — a guided snowshoe experience suitable for all ages. The First Flieger and Trottibike (mountain scooter on snow) are also great family-friendly options.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Grindelwald Glacier Gorge (Gletscherschlucht) — a dramatic ice gorge carved by the Lower Grindelwald Glacier. Entry is approximately CHF 8–10 per adult and CHF 5 for children. A unique, budget-friendly natural attraction that is unforgettable in winter. Afterward, explore the village and pop into local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost local event — check the Grindelwald tourist office board for live music, folklore evenings, or community events often held mid-week in winter season.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — Swiss-style muesli with milk, fruit, and yogurt (budget CHF 4–6 per person).
meals.lunch: Bergrestaurant Bort (mid-mountain on the First gondola line) — one of the more affordable mountain eateries with great views. Try the daily soup special and bread (budget CHF 12–16 per person).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Mercado in Grindelwald — offers a varied menu with Swiss and international dishes at mid-range prices. Look for the daily special (Tagesmenü) which includes soup, main, and sometimes dessert at a fixed budget price (CHF 22–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Glacier Gorge may have limited access in deep winter — confirm opening hours with the tourist office. First Flyer operates weather permitting. Book adventure activities at First online in advance to secure spots and sometimes get early-bird discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Männlichen — take the world's longest gondola cable car from Grindelwald Grund to Männlichen (included in ski pass). Ski the sunny Männlichen plateau, which offers some of the best beginner and intermediate terrain in the region with stunning panoramic views. Families with young children will love the wide, gentle slopes here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski from Männlichen down to Wengen via the Royal Ride — a classic, scenic blue run that is perfect for families and intermediate skiers. Walk around Wengen village, grab a warm drink, then take the Wengernalp Railway back to Grindelwald. Stop at Kleine Scheidegg for a quick photo stop with the iconic Eiger backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Toboggan run evening! The Grindelwald-First toboggan run is one of Switzerland's longest natural toboggan runs (approx. 15 km from First to Grindelwald). Evening toboggan sessions are sometimes available — check with the tourist office. Alternatively, rent sleds from the village and use the local sledding hills near the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — scrambled eggs, toast, juice, and coffee (budget CHF 5–8 per person).
meals.lunch: Berghaus Männlichen restaurant — try the affordable self-service section with soup and a roll, or a simple Bratwurst from the outdoor grill stand (budget CHF 10–15 per person).
meals.dinner: Gasthof Hirschen in Grindelwald — a traditional Swiss inn serving hearty local cuisine including cheese fondue, raclette, and rösti at very reasonable prices. Fondue for two approx. CHF 40–50 total.

day_by_day.notes: The Männlichen gondola from Grindelwald Grund is one of the longest in the world at 6.2 km — a spectacular ride in itself. The toboggan run from First requires taking the gondola up (included in ski pass during ski day). Evening toboggan sessions have separate fees — approximately CHF 15–20 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to Mürren — a spectacular car-free cliff-side village accessible by cable car and train from Grindelwald (via Lauterbrunnen). Ski the Schilthorn ski area above Mürren — famous for the James Bond film 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service.' The ski terrain here is more challenging with excellent off-piste options for advanced skiers, while families can enjoy the mid-mountain runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Piz Gloria revolving restaurant at the top of Schilthorn (2,970m) — the cable car up is an additional cost (approx. CHF 40–50 round trip from Mürren, not included in Jungfrau pass), but the 360-degree panoramic views of 200+ Alpine peaks including the Eiger, Mönch, Jungfrau, and even Mont Blanc on clear days are extraordinary. Consider this a splurge experience. Ski back down to Mürren.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald via Lauterbrunnen. Enjoy a final relaxed evening walk through the village. Visit the Grindelwald church viewpoint at dusk for spectacular Eiger views in the golden hour light.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — pack extra food for the day trip as Mürren prices are higher (bread, cheese, fruit, thermos of hot drink — budget CHF 5–8 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to eat on the slopes at Mürren — saves significantly compared to mountain restaurants in this area (budget CHF 8–12 per person).
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner on your penultimate night. Restaurant Schmitte in Grindelwald — traditional Swiss alpine cuisine with cheese fondue and local specialties. Budget CHF 30–40 per person for a special meal.

day_by_day.notes: Mürren is NOT included in the standard Jungfrau Ski Region pass — check your pass coverage carefully. The Schilthorn cable car from Mürren summit is separately ticketed. Travel to Mürren from Grindelwald takes approximately 1–1.5 hours via Lauterbrunnen — depart by 8:00 AM to maximize your day. Saturday can be busy — arrive at cable cars early.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning ski session — head back to Grindelwald-First for a few last runs on your favorite slopes. Take time to soak in the mountain views one last time. Return ski rental equipment by the agreed time (typically before 10:00–11:00 AM to avoid extra charges).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of accommodation (store luggage if needed). Take a final walk around Grindelwald village. Visit the Grindelwald Museum (Heimatmuseum) — a charming free or low-cost local history museum showcasing Alpine farming, climbing history, and traditional crafts. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping — Migros and Coop have affordable Swiss chocolate, cheese, and local products.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Grindelwald by train toward Zurich or your next destination. The train journey via Interlaken Ost to Zurich HB takes approximately 2.5–3 hours. If your flight is the next day, consider staying near Zurich Airport to save on morning travel stress.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast — use up remaining groceries from the fridge (budget CHF 4–6 per person).
meals.lunch: Grab a farewell lunch at the Coop Restaurant in Interlaken Ost during your train connection — a great affordable option for a final Swiss meal (budget CHF 12–18 per person).
meals.dinner: If departing late or staying near Zurich, try the Coop Restaurant at Zurich HB main station — excellent value Swiss food in a convenient location (budget CHF 15–22 per person). Alternatively, pick up Swiss chocolates and snacks for the journey home.

day_by_day.notes: Return ski passes if they are card-based and refundable. Keep all train tickets and receipts for expense tracking. Swiss chocolate from Migros or Coop is the best value souvenir — Lindt, Toblerone, and Frey brands are all excellent. The Swiss Travel Pass gives free travel on most trains, buses, and boats — verify coverage for your specific routes. Total estimated daily budget per person: CHF 80–130 (excluding ski pass and major lift tickets).

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00. Take the train from Zurich HB to Grindelwald (approx. 2.5 hours via Interlaken Ost). Check in to your boutique stay in Grindelwald-Wengen by approximately 16:00. Take a leisurely stroll through Grindelwald village, pick up ski passes and equipment rentals for the week, and get oriented with the Jungfrau ski area map.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the hotel, unpack, and enjoy a relaxed first evening. Take a short walk to admire the illuminated Eiger North Face at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Onboard the flight or at Zurich Airport — grab a coffee and pastry at a airport café (CHF 10–15).
meals.lunch: Light snack on the train or at Interlaken Ost station — try a Migros or Coop grab-and-go sandwich (CHF 8–12).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Mercado in Grindelwald — a cozy mid-range Alpine restaurant offering Swiss classics like Rösti and Zürcher Geschnetzeltes. Budget CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Jungfrau ski region multi-day lift pass at the resort or online in advance for best pricing. Consider renting ski equipment from Intersport in Grindelwald village for convenience. Swiss Travel Pass holders get discounts on trains from Zurich.

day_by_day.morning: First full day on the slopes! Head to the Grindelwald-First ski area, perfect for all skill levels. Enjoy wide groomed blue and red runs with stunning views of the Wetterhorn and Schreckhorn. Ski from 09:00 to 12:30 taking advantage of fresh morning snow conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the Jungfrau Region Slopes — transition to the Kleine Scheidegg area via ski lift, connecting Grindelwald with Wengen. Try the iconic Lauberhorn run, one of the longest ski descents in the region. Beginners in the family can take a group ski lesson (available through the Swiss Ski School, bookable at the base station).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village by 16:30. Warm up with a hot chocolate at a mountain café before heading back to the hotel. Enjoy a relaxed family evening with board games or a swim if the hotel has wellness facilities.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Café 3692 in Grindelwald — fresh bread, Swiss cheese, cold cuts, and coffee. Budget CHF 15–20 per person.
meals.lunch: Mountain lunch at Bergrestaurant Bort on the First plateau — hearty Alpine soup, Käseschnitte (Swiss cheese toast), and warm drinks. Budget CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Spinne's Gepsi-Bar & Restaurant — popular with locals and families, serving fondue, pasta, and grilled meats in a warm chalet atmosphere. Budget CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Swiss Ski School group lessons at least one day in advance, especially during peak February school holidays. Dress in moisture-wicking base layers, insulating mid-layers, and waterproof outer shells. Apply high-SPF sunscreen — Alpine UV reflection off snow is intense even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Swiss Cheese & Fondue Cooking Experience — join a hands-on traditional Swiss fondue and raclette cooking class in a cozy Alpine chalet near Grindelwald. Learn to select and blend Gruyère and Emmental cheeses, master the fondue technique, and discover the history behind Switzerland's most iconic dish. Classes typically run 09:30–12:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cooking class, enjoy the afternoon on the Grindelwald-Wengen ski slopes. Take the Männlichen gondola from Grindelwald for a scenic ride up and ski the long, gentle runs back down — ideal for families with mixed skill levels. The Männlichen plateau also offers breathtaking panoramic views of the Jungfrau massif.
day_by_day.evening: Tobogganing on a local run — the Grindelwald area has excellent evening toboggan runs, some illuminated at night. Rent a toboggan from the village and enjoy a thrilling family descent before warming up indoors.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — fuel up before the cooking class with a full Swiss breakfast spread.
meals.lunch: Taste the fruits of your labor! The fondue cooking class typically includes a full tasting lunch of everything prepared during the session (included in class fee, approx. CHF 80–100 per person).
meals.dinner: Light dinner at a local pizzeria or pub — try Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald for wood-fired pizzas and casual Alpine dining. Budget CHF 20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Swiss Cheese & Fondue Cooking Experience should be pre-booked as class sizes are limited, especially during peak winter season. Fondue etiquette tip: if you drop your bread in the pot, tradition says you owe the table a round of drinks! Evening toboggan runs in Grindelwald are typically open until 22:00 on select nights — verify schedule locally.

day_by_day.morning: Family Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking — take an early morning train from Grindelwald to explore the winter landscape on a guided family snowshoeing tour. The trails around the Jungfrau region wind through snow-laden forests and open meadows with spectacular mountain backdrops. Guides provide all equipment and the pace is family-friendly. Tours typically depart 09:00 and last 3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snowshoeing, visit the Jungfraujoch — the 'Top of Europe' at 3,454m. Take the cogwheel train from Kleine Scheidegg to Jungfraujoch station. Explore the Ice Palace, the Sphinx Observatory viewing platform, and the Snow Fun Park where kids can try snow tubing and ziplines. Allow 3–4 hours for the full experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxed spa or wellness evening at the hotel or a nearby thermal facility. Some boutique hotels in the region offer sauna and steam room access.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the snowshoeing tour — pack energy bars and a thermos of hot tea for the trail.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jungfraujoch — Crystal Restaurant or Self-Service Restaurant at the Top of Europe. Expect elevated prices at altitude; budget CHF 25–40 per person for a hot meal.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Firestarter in Grindelwald — known for its relaxed atmosphere, craft beers, and hearty burgers and Alpine dishes. Budget CHF 25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Jungfraujoch tickets should be booked well in advance online — prices are approximately CHF 145–175 per adult and CHF 80–90 per child with a Swiss Travel Pass discount. Altitude sickness can affect some visitors at 3,454m — take it slow, stay hydrated, and allow time to acclimatize. Bring an extra warm layer as temperatures at the summit can drop to -15°C or below even in mild conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride — depart early from Grindelwald toward Zermatt by connecting train, then board the legendary Glacier Express panoramic train. The 8-hour scenic journey through the Swiss Alps passes 291 bridges, 91 tunnels, and the iconic Oberalp Pass. Book the morning departure to maximize daylight scenery. This is a full-day excursion away from the base.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Glacier Express journey through the Rhône Valley, Goms region, and dramatic Alpine gorges. Enjoy the panoramic windows and onboard commentary. Arrive in Zermatt by mid-to-late afternoon. Take a brief walk through car-free Zermatt village and admire the Matterhorn before the return journey or overnight if preferred.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald via train from Zermatt (approximately 3 hours via Visp and Interlaken). Alternatively, if budget allows, enjoy dinner in Zermatt before heading back. Arrive back at the hotel by 21:00–22:00.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — pack snacks for the train.
meals.lunch: Onboard dining on the Glacier Express — the restaurant car serves a set lunch menu featuring regional Swiss dishes. Pre-book the dining car reservation when purchasing your train ticket. Budget CHF 40–55 per person including a drink.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Zermatt before return — try Restaurant Whymper-Stube for traditional Swiss cuisine in a historic setting near the Matterhorn Museum. Budget CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Glacier Express reservations are mandatory and must be booked in advance through SBB (Swiss Federal Railways) or the Glacier Express website. Seat reservation fee is approximately CHF 13–49 per person depending on class. Swiss Travel Pass holders travel free but still pay the reservation fee. Window seats on the right side of the train (traveling from Zermatt to St. Moritz direction) offer the best mountain views. This is a long day — pack water, snacks, entertainment for children, and a good camera.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the long train day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Then head to the slopes for a half-day of skiing on the Grindelwald-Wengen Jungfrau Region runs — focus on favorite runs from earlier in the week and let the family ski freely at their own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run — for an exciting change of pace, take a day trip to experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling natural toboggan runs, stretching over 3km through Alpine terrain. The journey from Grindelwald to Maienfeld takes approximately 1.5 hours by train. The run is suitable for older children and adults and offers a unique non-ski winter thrill.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by early evening. Enjoy a farewell fondue dinner as a family — book a restaurant with traditional pot fondue for a proper Swiss send-off experience.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel — take your time and enjoy the full spread.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the toboggan run at a local Beizli (Swiss pub) in Maienfeld — try regional Graubünden specialties like Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) and Maluns. Budget CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell fondue dinner at Restaurant Chalet-Hotel Gydisdorf or similar traditional chalet restaurant in Grindelwald. Order the classic cheese fondue moitié-moitié (half Gruyère, half Vacherin). Budget CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Fläsch-Maienfeld toboggan run is weather and snow-dependent — check conditions before making the trip. Toboggans can be rented at the top of the run for approximately CHF 10–15. Helmets are recommended especially for children. Saturday slopes can be busier — try to hit the lifts early (before 10:00) to avoid peak crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — wake up early for one last sunrise view of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau from the village. Take a short, easy winter walk through Grindelwald village to pick up souvenirs: Swiss chocolate, local cheese, carved wooden gifts, and Swiss Army knives from village shops. Pack and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final light lunch in Grindelwald before taking the train back toward Zurich Airport. The journey from Grindelwald to Zurich HB takes approximately 2.5 hours. Allow at least 2 hours at the airport before your international departure. If time allows, browse the duty-free shops at Zurich Airport for last-minute Swiss chocolate and watches.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Zurich Airport. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, mountain scenery, Swiss cuisine, and family memories in the Jungfrau Region.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy the full Swiss spread one last time: fresh bread, local cheeses, Birchermüesli, and strong Swiss coffee.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Café Bar 3692 or Bäckerei Fleischmann in Grindelwald village — enjoy a Gipfeli (Swiss croissant), open-faced sandwich, and coffee before boarding the train. Budget CHF 15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Zurich Airport — Zurich HB and the airport have excellent dining options including Hiltl (world's oldest vegetarian restaurant) and various Swiss and international options. Budget CHF 25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at most Swiss boutique hotels is 11:00 — arrange luggage storage at the hotel if your train departs later. Swiss trains are extremely punctual — arrive at the platform at least 5 minutes before departure. Validate any unused rail tickets before departure. Consider purchasing Swiss chocolate at Läderach or Lindt shops in Zurich Airport as premium gifts — prices are comparable to or better than city center shops.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Allow time for luggage collection, customs, and private transfer to Grindelwald-Wengen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from the airport to your boutique stay in Grindelwald-Wengen (approximately 2–2.5 hours). Upon arrival, enjoy a private welcome orientation with your concierge, unpack, and settle into your suite. Take a leisurely stroll along the village promenade to soak in your first Alpine views and get your bearings for the week ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant or a highly-regarded local establishment such as Restaurant Schmitte in Grindelwald — known for its warm Alpine ambiance and refined Swiss cuisine. Toast to the trip with a glass of Swiss Chasselas white wine.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at Zurich Airport before or after customs — try Zurich Airport's Marché Mövenpick for fresh Swiss fare
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schmitte, Grindelwald — indulge in Alpine classics such as Berner Rösti, pan-seared lake trout, and a fondue starter in a cozy, candlelit chalet setting

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer (e.g., a Mercedes V-Class or similar) through your hotel concierge for a seamless arrival experience. Confirm ski equipment rental or purchase appointments for Day 2 during check-in. Ensure lift passes are pre-booked for the Jungfrau region to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day introduction to Skiing on the Jungfrau Region Slopes — begin your morning with a private ski guide meeting at First or Kleine Scheidegg. Warm up on the wide, groomed blue and red runs of Grindelwald First, with breathtaking views of the Eiger North Face. A private ski instructor is recommended for family members of varying skill levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing through the interconnected Jungfrau Ski Region, exploring runs toward Wengen and Männlichen. Enjoy a mid-afternoon pause at a high-altitude mountain restaurant for hot chocolate and a light Alpine snack before a final run back to the valley.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for a relaxing soak or spa treatment if available. Dinner at a premium local restaurant — consider Brasserie Grindelwald or the Grand Hotel Regina's fine dining room for a sophisticated multi-course Alpine menu.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss breakfast buffet at the hotel — featuring local cheeses, cold cuts, fresh-baked bread, bircher muesli, and hot dishes
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Berghaus Bort or a Jungfrau mountain hut on the slopes — try the house rösti, Alpine soup, and warm apple strudel
meals.dinner: Grand Hotel Regina Fine Dining, Grindelwald — seasonal tasting menu with wine pairing; expect dishes like venison medallions, truffle risotto, and Swiss chocolate fondant

day_by_day.notes: Book a certified private ski instructor through the Swiss Ski School (Grindelwald) in advance. Ensure all family members are fitted with properly sized rental equipment the evening before or first thing in the morning. Lift passes for the Jungfrau region cover Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren — purchase multi-day passes for best value.

day_by_day.morning: Family Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking experience — embark on a guided family snowshoeing tour departing from the Grindelwald-Wengen area. A private guide will lead you through snow-draped forests and open meadows, pointing out local wildlife tracks, Alpine flora, and stunning Jungfrau panoramas. Suitable for all ages and fitness levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the snowshoeing tour, head to a traditional Alpine chalet for the Swiss Cheese & Fondue Cooking Experience. A local culinary expert will teach the family the art of making authentic Swiss cheese fondue and raclette — from selecting the right cheeses (Gruyère, Emmental, Appenzeller) to mastering the perfect melt. Everyone gets hands-on time stirring the pot!
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fondue and raclette you've prepared together as a family dinner in the chalet setting — a truly memorable and immersive Swiss cultural experience. Return to the hotel for a quiet evening with hot drinks by the fireplace.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the hotel — freshly squeezed juices, eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, and Swiss pastries
meals.lunch: Light picnic-style lunch provided during the snowshoeing tour by the guide — thermos of hot soup, artisan sandwiches, Swiss chocolate, and local dried fruits
meals.dinner: The fondue and raclette prepared during the cooking class served in the Alpine chalet — accompanied by local charcuterie, cornichons, pearl onions, and Swiss white wine (Fendant)

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoes and poles are typically provided by the guide service — confirm in advance. The fondue cooking class can be arranged through local operators such as 'Swiss Alpine Guides' or via the hotel concierge. This is an ideal rest-day activity for leg recovery between ski days. Children will particularly enjoy both the snowshoeing and the cooking experience.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Jungfrau Region Slopes for a more ambitious ski day — take the Jungfraujoch cogwheel train from Grindelwald or Wengen up to Europe's highest railway station (3,454m) for a spectacular morning ski descent on high-alpine terrain. The views of the Aletsch Glacier from the top are unmissable. Experienced skiers can tackle the challenging runs from Eigergletscher.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tobogganing on a local natural toboggan run near Grindelwald or the famous Fläsch-Maienfeld style run — an exhilarating 3km+ descent through Alpine forest and meadows. Sleds can be rented locally, and the run is accessible by lift. This is a perfect family activity that combines thrills with stunning scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski cocktails at a stylish mountain bar in Grindelwald village — try the Mescalito Bar or the hotel bar for craft cocktails and live music. Follow with an intimate dinner at a premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast buffet — energy-rich options including porridge, eggs, smoked meats, and fresh fruit to fuel a high-altitude ski morning
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe restaurant or the Eigergletscher mountain restaurant — hot Alpine soups, grilled meats, and panoramic glacier views
meals.dinner: Restaurant Alte Post, Grindelwald — a beloved fine dining institution offering refined Swiss-French cuisine; signature dishes include lake perch meunière, Berner Platte, and chocolate marquise

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfraujoch excursion requires booking train tickets well in advance, especially in peak February season. Altitude (3,454m) can cause mild symptoms — stay hydrated and ascend slowly. The toboggan run is best experienced in the afternoon when the snow is slightly softer. Helmets are strongly recommended for tobogganing, especially for children.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride — depart early from the Grindelwald/Interlaken area and connect to board the legendary Glacier Express panoramic train. This iconic 8-hour journey connects Zermatt to St. Moritz through some of Switzerland's most dramatic Alpine landscapes, crossing 291 bridges and 91 tunnels. Book first-class or Excellence Class seats for the ultimate premium experience with gourmet on-board dining.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Glacier Express journey through the Rhône Valley, Oberalp Pass, and Graubünden highlands. Enjoy the ever-changing scenery from your panoramic windows — snow-capped peaks, frozen rivers, and remote Alpine villages. Arrive in St. Moritz or enjoy a partial journey before returning, depending on your preference.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey or private transfer back to Grindelwald-Wengen. A relaxed evening at the hotel with an in-room premium dining option or a quiet dinner at a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — croissants, yogurt, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet on-board dining in the Glacier Express Excellence Class — a curated multi-course lunch with regional specialties, Swiss wines, and impeccable service served at your panoramic window seat
meals.dinner: In-room dining at the boutique stay — request a curated cheese and charcuterie board, warm soup, and a bottle of Swiss Pinot Noir for a relaxed, intimate evening after a long travel day

day_by_day.notes: The Glacier Express requires advance reservation — book Excellence Class or 1st Class seats months ahead during peak winter season. A full Zermatt-to-St. Moritz journey takes approximately 8 hours; consider a partial route if preferred. This is a lighter physical day, ideal for resting legs mid-week. Children will be captivated by the dramatic mountain scenery throughout the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final full ski day on the Jungfrau Region Slopes — make the most of your last ski day by exploring any runs not yet covered, particularly the Mürren-Schilthorn area accessible via Lauterbrunnen. The Schilthorn (2,970m), famously featured in the James Bond film 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service,' offers dramatic skiing and a revolving Piz Gloria restaurant at the summit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon skiing with a focus on family favorites — revisit the most-loved runs of the week. Consider a private family ski photo session with a mountain photographer for lasting memories. Return equipment to rental shop by late afternoon and store skis for the final time.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at one of Grindelwald's or Wengen's finest establishments — book a private dining room if available. Celebrate the week's adventures with a premium tasting menu, champagne, and a dessert platter. Consider gifting the family a Swiss chocolate selection or local artisan souvenirs from village shops before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full hotel breakfast — take your time and enjoy every Swiss specialty on offer before the final ski day
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Piz Gloria revolving restaurant on the Schilthorn summit — an iconic 007-themed dining experience with panoramic 360-degree Alpine views and classic Swiss dishes
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Hotel Belvedere Grindelwald or a comparable luxury establishment — premium 5-course tasting menu featuring dishes like foie gras terrine, Wagyu beef, truffle pasta, artisan Swiss cheese board, and a Grand Marnier soufflé; paired with a curated wine flight

day_by_day.notes: The Schilthorn and Piz Gloria restaurant should be reserved well in advance. A mountain photographer can often be arranged through the Swiss Ski School or private guides — this makes for an exceptional keepsake. Use the afternoon to purchase any last-minute Swiss souvenirs: Lindt chocolates, local honey, Appenzeller cheese, or Swiss Army knives from village boutiques.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Grindelwald-Wengen — enjoy a long, relaxed breakfast at the hotel. Take a gentle post-ski walk through the village one last time, breathing in the Alpine air and admiring the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks. Visit any remaining boutiques or the local market for last-minute Swiss specialties and gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer departs from the hotel to Zurich Airport (or your onward destination). Allow ample time — approximately 2.5 to 3 hours — accounting for luggage, mountain road conditions, and airport check-in. Enjoy the scenic drive through the Bernese Oberland as a final farewell to the Alps.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. If your flight is late evening, enjoy a final Swiss meal at Zurich Airport's upper-level restaurants or the SWISS First Class Lounge if eligible.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final hotel breakfast — order everything you loved during the week, from bircher muesli to fresh Alpine cheese and warm croissants; perhaps enjoy it with a glass of fresh-pressed apple juice overlooking the mountains
meals.lunch: Light lunch en route or at Zurich Airport — try Zurich Airport's Mesa Restaurant or Clouds Restaurant on the 35th floor of Prime Tower nearby if time permits before check-in
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport dining depending on departure time — if flying SWISS Business or First Class, enjoy their award-winning in-flight Swiss cuisine with a final glass of Swiss wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transfer the night before to confirm pickup time. Luggage storage at the hotel can be used if checkout is before the transfer. Swiss customs allow generous duty-free allowances for chocolates and regional food products. Ensure ski equipment is properly packed if taking personal gear home. Keep travel documents, lift passes (some have souvenir value), and any receipts for VAT refund claims accessible at the airport.

query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February 2026
